title: Which quotients follow from one division fact?
description: Seven hundred fifty six divided by thirty six is twenty one. The video uses this one fact to find six related quotients, by moving the decimal point in the dividend and the divisor and seeing how the quotient changes.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same shift in both numbers keeps the quotient, and a shift in only one number shifts the quotient by the same number of places. Ask the class what seventy five point six divided by three point six could be before any work is shown. Watch for students who move the point in one number and forget the other. The sixth division is the same as the second one in the book.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q8
video_script.why: The child can use a known multiplication fact to place the decimal point in a product, and now uses a known division fact to find related quotients.
video_script.substitution: The dividend and the divisor are each written as the known numbers times or divided by ten, a hundred or a thousand, and the quotient follows.
video_script.anchor: The fact 756 ÷ 36 = 21 and six divisions to find from it
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty one, twenty one, two thousand one hundred, zero point two one, two thousand one hundred, twenty one

final_answer.spoken: twenty one, twenty one, two thousand one hundred, zero point two one, two thousand one hundred, twenty one

maths_rules: the sixth division is the same as the second, so it is 21
video_script.design: One idea: shift the decimal point by the same number of places in both numbers and the quotient is unchanged; shift only one and the quotient shifts. The fact and the six divisions stay on the board all video; the working band takes the six divisions one at a time.
open_questions: The book lists the same division 7.56 ÷ 0.36 twice, as the second and the sixth part. The video answers both and says they are the same.
